dedupe_keys.name: altis sentinel 1 sar pipeline for property level flood damage triage

description: ALTIS, Automated Loss Triage and Impact Scoring, is a five-stage pipeline that turns Sentinel-1 radar imagery into property-level flood impact scores within 24 to 48 hours of the flood peak, aimed at insurance claims triage. Stages: multi-temporal SAR change detection using dual-polarisation intensity and InSAR coherence; physics-informed flood depth estimation that fuses flood extent with high-resolution elevation data; property-level zonal statistics from parcel footprints; depth-damage calibration against National Flood Insurance Program claims, with default Hazus parameters when claims are not yet available; and confidence-scored ranking. The authors define Insurance-Grade Flood Triage and two metrics, the Inspection Reduction Rate and Triage Efficiency Score. Using Hurricane Harvey (2017) in Harris County, Texas, they report preliminary results suggesting an inspection reduction rate of about 0.52 at 90% recall of high-severity claims. The preprint is marked preliminary, with full end-to-end validation ongoing. Access: paper only (CC BY 4.0); no code link found. Inputs come from open sources: Sentinel-1, OpenFEMA claims, USGS high-water marks and county parcel data. It builds on the Hazus method in the catalogue, and serves exposure and emergency response planning.
